verses.text: LORD, remember what has happened to us. Look and see our disgrace.
Our land has been handed over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
We have become orphans without fathers. Our mothers are like widows.
We have to pay for the water we drink. We have to buy our own firewood.
Our enemies are right on our heels. We are worn out and have no rest.
We made deals with Egypt and Assyria to get enough bread to eat.
Our ancestors sinned and are gone, and we are paying for their sins.
Slaves rule over us, and no one can rescue us from their power.
We risk our lives to get bread, because of the sword in the desert.
Our skin is as hot as an oven from the fever of hunger.
Women were raped in Zion, young women in the towns of Judah.
Leaders were hung up by their hands. Elders were shown no respect.
Young men are forced to grind grain at the mill. Boys stagger under loads of wood.
The elders no longer sit at the city gate. The young men have stopped their music.
The joy has gone from our hearts. Our dancing has turned to mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. How terrible for us, because we have sinned!
Because of this our hearts are sick. Because of these things our eyes grow dim,
because Mount Zion lies empty, and jackals roam over it.
But you, LORD, rule forever. Your throne lasts from generation to generation.
Why do you keep forgetting us? Why have you abandoned us for so long?
Bring us back to you, LORD, so that we can return. Make our lives new again, as they were long ago.
Unless you have completely rejected us and are angry with us beyond measure.
